organizer: Genç Başarı Eğitim Vakfı (Junior Achievement Türkiye)
prerequisites: Students participate in teams, verbatim: '5-10 kişilik ekipleri'. Applications are accepted from students, teachers, alumni and business-world volunteer mentors.
cost_note: No participation fee is stated on the page. The page states students found their companies 'sıfır sermaye ile' (with zero capital) — that describes the company's starting capital, NOT a programme fee, and must not be read as 'free'.
award_or_output: Students found a small-scale real company inside school, produce and sell a real product/service, and may earn the Entrepreneurial Skills Pass (ESP) certificate.

sources.title: GençBizz — Genç Başarı Eğitim Vakfı
sources.supports: 13–18 age range, 5–10 person teams, zero-capital company model, ESP certificate, who may apply

research_notes: VERIFIED on the organizer's own page: age range 13–18, team size 5–10, the real-company-inside-school model, the ESP certificate, and the applicant types. NOT VERIFIED and deliberately left null: application dates, deadline, programme duration, participation fee, and the academic cycle year — none appear on the programme page. A Turkish education-news aggregator described a '2025-2026 uygulama dönemi' call; that is aggregator-only and is NOT recorded as fact. AMBIGUITY: the page does not state whether a student can apply individually or only through a participating school with an advisor teacher; the presence of a teacher application route suggests school mediation is required, but this is inference, not verified. RELATIONSHIP: Genç Başarı is the Türkiye member of the JA Europe network, so GençBizz appears to be the Turkish national implementation of the JA Company Programme (separate record in this batch). They should be kept as distinct rows — different eligible ages (13–18 vs 15–18) and different application routes — but the ingestion lane should link them rather than treat one as a duplicate of the other.

prerequisites: Delivered through schools; the official page gives only a contact address (info@jaeurope.org) and does not publish an individual student application route.
cost_note: No pricing or cost information appears on the official programme page.
selection_process: Not a selective admissions programme; participation is via school. Teams compete in 'company-of-the-year competitions'.
award_or_output: Students elect a board of directors, raise share capital, conduct market research, build a business plan, develop and trade a real product/service, manage finances and compete. Verbatim scale: 'Every year, over 360,000 students enrolled in the programme, creating 30,000 mini-companies'. The page references the 'Entrepreneurial Skills Pass'.

sources.title: JA Company Programme — JA Europe
sources.supports: age range 15–18, one-academic-year duration, 360,000 students / 30,000 mini-companies, activity description, ESP reference, contact route

research_notes: CONFLICT RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED: the official JA Europe programme page states 'students aged 15-18'. Multiple secondary sources (including an ILO-hosted JA-YE document and EIT materials) state 'aged 15-19'. I have recorded the organizer's own figure (15–18) and am flagging the discrepancy rather than silently choosing — the 19 figure may reflect older programme documentation or national variants. NOT VERIFIED: cost, deadlines, the country list, and whether a student can join without their school participating. The page publishes no application form, only info@jaeurope.org, which means ORYN cannot give a student a direct 'apply here' action for this record — the honest student-facing action is 'ask your school whether it runs JA'. DEDUP: overlaps conceptually with GençBizz (Türkiye national implementation, separate record) and with any national JA/Young Enterprise rows ORYN may already hold.
